description: A regulatory legal director must approve the company's response to a regulator's inquiry into alleged procurement misconduct, including whether to make a voluntary disclosure, what investigation materials to produce, and how to address a conflict involving the existing investigator.

shared_context.S1: A state regulator has requested the company's internal-investigation materials concerning alleged improper procurement practices.
shared_context.S2: The regulator's response deadline is ten business days from the date of the request.
shared_context.S3: The current draft response proposes continuing with the existing investigation, providing a general status update, and preserving all potentially privileged material.
shared_context.S4: Before approving the response, Elena conducts the firm's routine pre-submission review and asks compliance counsel and conflicts counsel to report any issues affecting the filing.

PF1.text: Samir confirmed with the regulator's staff this week that its cooperation protocol grants credit only if the company makes a voluntary disclosure by the fifth business day after the review meeting, produces factual interview summaries, and withholds legal advice and attorney work product; he has not circulated the confirmation because it arrived after the response draft was prepared.

PF2.text: Maya's conflict review found that the company's existing investigator previously represented a procurement witness in an unrelated matter involving the same allegations, so the investigator must be removed and the factual investigation must be re-performed by an independent investigator; she has not updated the matter's conflict log because the review was completed this morning.

acceptance_conditions: The company must make a voluntary disclosure.
The voluntary disclosure must be made within exactly five business days after the review meeting.
The response must provide factual interview summaries.
The response must withhold legal advice and attorney work product.
The existing investigator must be removed.
An independent reinvestigation must be required.
The settlement must commit to the independent reinvestigation.

decisive_facts.why: The existing draft calls for a general update and blanket privilege protection, while PF1 changes the response to a voluntary disclosure on exactly the fifth business day with factual summaries produced and legal advice and work product withheld.

The existing draft assumes the current investigation can continue, while PF2 changes the staffing decision to remove the conflicted investigator and require an independent reinvestigation, which must be reflected as the independent_reinvestigation_required decision.
